title: Check directional word pairs against page-cluster reversals and position-only templates
statement: Use the released directional_pairs count with W=3, K=1 including cutoff ties, and strictly more than five directional occurrences of excess. In 20 stationary reversible-persistence sequences, global, page and line shuffles all reject 20/20 at .05; independent page reversals reject 1/20. For planted directed rings with independently randomized page orientations the counts are 20/20, 20/20, 18/20, 2/20 in the same null order. All four nulls reject 20/20 stationary directed-ring controls with common orientation and 20/20 texts generated by three independent position-dependent vocabulary bands. A rejection can therefore reflect line templates. IID Zipf and page/line vocabulary mixtures reject 0–2/20 across nulls. Exact equal counts at K=1 remove every token, leaving all 20 documents unsupported. K=0 restores support, with 1/20 rejections under each null. Cutoff ties, whole-book and page and line shuffles, and the reversal test each preserve the word multiset. Five historical pin windows from three works, including two anchored body windows, give p=.01 with every null in the original, clean substitution and circa 2% character corruption. One preselected Latin pin provides 4,895 words and is unavailable under the 5,000-word protocol. Six exact relabeling comparisons and 206 count oracle checks pass.
check: Reproduce control counts with the stored fixed generator parameters and seeds. To use a reversal null on manuscript witnesses, first calibrate controls with real line and page inventories and fixed position roles, and state the exchangeable orientation assumption at the page level. A position-conditional null should compare the same line slots across nearby lines while preserving the marginal position profile. Measure sensitivity to pages with different line counts, order-specific topics, and cipher substitutions with more than one ciphertext per input symbol. Assign separate support outcomes for tied cutoffs and inert draws before running any manuscript test.
protocol:
# P-J-039, fixed public-control protocol

No manuscript text or hidden split. Each synthetic document has 50 pages of
10 lines of ten words, 5,000 tokens. Twenty independent documents per
scenario, NumPy PCG64 seeds 8200–8219. Measure the released statistic,
W=3 positions after compressing removed stops within a line, strict
absolute directional pair-count difference >5, observed unequal unordered
pair type denominator. Primary K=1 removes all ties at the maximum count.
K=0 is a frozen sensitivity for tied-max and fully balanced documents.
Under 30 surviving tokens or 30 pair types is unsupported.

For each scenario compare 99 whole-document, within-page, within-line,
and page-cluster reversal randomizations with separately reset PCG64 seeds
408, 409, 410, 411. Whole-document and within-page shuffles refill the
same line lengths. Page reversal flips the direction of every line on a
page jointly, independently with probability 1/2 and preserves unsigned
within-line distance counts. Use (1 + number >= observed) / 100; undefined
draws count against the claim and unchanged nulls are flagged inert.
Report Wilson 95% intervals for rejections per independent synthetic
document, plus support and inert status. Tests are separate diagnostics.

Synthetic scenarios: iid 80 categories with rank^(-0.85) probabilities;
exchangeable fixed counts with four maximizers of count 300 and 76 types
of count 50; exchangeable perfectly balanced 50 types of count 100;
page- or line-mixture iid with random topic-specific permutation of the
global Zipf probabilities per block; stationary persistent process that
repeats with probability .8 and otherwise redraws from Zipf; stationary
asymmetric process that advances within an eight-type ring with probability
.82 and otherwise redraws, with equal weights within each ring, 10 rings,
unequal mass between rings; and a position template using three disjoint
sets of 20 equiprobable types in respective line bands 3/4/3.
The two transition processes restart each line from the stationary marginal.

Historical titles fixed in advance: Erasmus's Encomium artis medicae,
Villon's Oeuvres completes, Chaucer's Canterbury Tales and Other Poems,
and the Postilla of Jan Hus, the first 5,000 normalized words from each
individual pin with the same artificial layout. Compare plaintext,
fixed bijective character substitution, and 2% independent character
replacement on that ciphertext by a different symbol chosen uniformly.
Use identical shuffle indices across modes and verify exact plaintext and
clean substitution invariance. No cipher search or inference about genres
from these four books. If a pin has fewer than 5,000 words it is reported
unavailable for this comparison, without substituting another title.
supplementary_protocol:
# Declared supplementary controls

The main fixed 5,000-word pin windows include editorial introductions in
the French and English pins and the Erasmus pin is too short. Separately
anchor windows to the opening of Villon's Grand Testament ("En l'an
trentiesme de mon aage") and Chaucer's General Prologue ("WHEN that Aprilis,
with his showers swoot"), then use 5,000 normalized words after that marker.
Remove a right column after a run of at least four spaces, numbered inline
angle-bracket references, and bracketed folio pages before normalization.
The old editions may still contain notes or glosses. Keep Erasmus as
unavailable and do not vary the frozen main windows.

Add a clustered sign control to test page-level reversal itself. Use the
same within-page directed-rings process as the original positive control.
Independently reverse all 10 lines in each page with probability 1/2 from
a separate NumPy PCG64 generator seeded 18200–18219. The null of independent
page orientations is true by construction even with substantial local order.
Score with all four nulls under the original K=1 and protocol.
